description: Two concrete recommendations follow from the survey's knowledge and retrieval findings.
title: Provide students with a faculty-level list of EBM-related terms and explicitly teach the use of PubMed/Medline and the Cochrane Library

description: The authors observed that students reported fast searches but low satisfaction with results, possibly because they searched primary databases like PubMed or single journals, leading to overly broad or narrow yields.
title: EBM training should emphasize efficient searching by focusing on appropriate clinical information sources

title: Administer the EBMQ to help policy makers identify knowledge, practice and barrier gaps and improve EBM uptake

description: The article recommends interactive E-book apps as an in-service education strategy for nurses facing workload and staffing barriers to face-to-face courses.
title: Offer interactive E-book apps for nurses' self-paced in-service education

description: The authors recommend combining eBooks with standard teacher-led classes so that classroom learning through an expert is complemented by \"additional independent directed interactive learning outside the classroom\".
title: Use interactive eBooks as an adjunct to traditional teaching rather than a substitute

title: Incorporate role modeling, time for reflection, and social small-group strategies into undergraduate EBP curricula

title: Support EBP education with mentorship, protected time, and continuity of initiatives rather than isolated courses
